name: Mount Pelee
title: Mount Pelee: 1902 Eruption, Activity Now, Height & Facts
description: Mount Pelee destroyed the city of Saint-Pierre in 1902. It last erupted in 1932, and its observatory has kept it on yellow alert while it stirs again. Dates, sources and the full record.
lede: On May 8, 1902, an avalanche of hot gas and ash from this volcano destroyed the city of Saint-Pierre in two to three minutes and killed about 28,000 people. The volcano has not erupted since 1932, but its observatory has recorded a reawakening since 2019 and keeps it on yellow alert. Below: what the instruments show now, what happened in 1902, and every eruption on record.
answer: **Mount Pelee last erupted from {last_start} to {last_end}.**[[gvp]] It is a **stratovolcano** on the French island of Martinique, in the Caribbean, **{summit_ft} ft ({summit_m} m)** high.[[gvp]][[vw1902]] In the newest weekly report on its observatory’s list, dated November 13, 2026, the alert level is yellow, the second of four.[[ipgplist]][[ovsm]] In French the volcano is the Montagne Pelée.

paras: Mount Pelee is on Martinique, a French island in the Lesser Antilles, the arc of islands on the eastern side of the Caribbean, at {coords}.[[gvp]][[vw1902]] Saint-Pierre, the city it destroyed in 1902, is on the coast nearby.[[usgsfaq]] It is one of {n_country} volcanoes in [France](/volcanoes-in-france) on the Smithsonian’s Holocene list, which counts French territory overseas.[[gvp]]

It is not erupting, and it is not asleep. The Martinique volcano observatory, run by the Institut de physique du globe de Paris, describes a reactivation that began in April 2019, when earthquakes under the volcano rose above their usual level.[[ovsm]]

Other signs followed. From late 2019 patches of vegetation died back on the southwest flank, where carbon dioxide seeps out of the soil. The summit swelled slightly from mid-2021 to the end of 2022. It began to swell again in September 2025, and faster from the end of April 2026.[[ovsm]]
In September 2026 the observatory counted 655 volcanic earthquakes. Nobody reported feeling any of them, and the largest had a magnitude of 1.96.[[ovsm]]

The alert level is **yellow**, which stands for vigilance. It is the second of four levels: green, yellow, orange and red.[[ovsm]] It was still yellow in the newest weekly report on the observatory’s list, dated November 13, 2026.[[ipgplist]]
The observatory rates the chance of an eruption in the short term as low. It adds that it cannot rule out a change over weeks, months or years.[[ovsm]]

The Smithsonian dates the eruption from April 23, 1902 to October 5, 1905.[[gvp]] Its deadliest day was **May 8, 1902**. A pyroclastic flow, a fast avalanche of hot gas, ash and rock, swept down from the volcano and over the coastal city of Saint-Pierre.[[vw1902]][[usgsfaq]]

USGS puts the destruction of the city at two to three minutes and the deaths at 28,000.[[vw1902]] Another USGS page says nearly 30,000.[[usgsfaq]] NOAA’s database lists {worst_deaths} deaths for {worst_date}.[[noaa]]
It happened one day after the Soufrière volcano on St. Vincent, 100 miles (150 km) to the south, killed 2,000 people. The timing was a coincidence.[[vw1902]]
May 8 was neither the first deadly day nor the last. NOAA has six entries for the volcano in 1902, and those for May 5 and August 30 also record deaths.[[noaa]]
The deadly cloud was new to the science of the day, which named it a nuée ardente, French for glowing cloud. Volcanologists now call it a pyroclastic flow.[[vw1929]][[usgsfaq]]

sections.h: When did Mount Pelee last erupt?
paras: Mount Pelee’s last eruption ran from **{last_start} to {last_end}** in the Smithsonian’s record.[[gvp]]

A lava dome grew slowly at the summit. From time to time parts of it collapsed and sent pyroclastic flows down a valley on the volcano’s side. The eruption was less explosive than the one of 1902 and lasted longer, which made it easier for scientists to study.[[vw1929]]
The observatory dates the end of that eruption to 1932. The last steam vents on the volcano stopped in 1970.[[ovsm]]
Mount Pelee is **{summit_ft} ft ({summit_m} m)** high on the Smithsonian’s list.[[gvp]]

sections.h: What type of volcano is Mount Pelee?
paras: Mount Pelee is a **[stratovolcano](/types-of-volcanoes)**.[[gvp]] Its observatory calls it an active volcano of the explosive type, with eruptions of magma and eruptions driven by steam in its past.[[ovsm]] The Smithsonian lists its main rock as {rock}.[[gvp]]

sections.h: How often does Mount Pelee erupt?
paras: The Smithsonian’s list has **{n_all} confirmed eruptions**, most of them dated from their deposits. It rates {n_vei4} of them VEI 4 on the [Volcanic Explosivity Index](/volcanic-explosivity-index), the eruption of 1902 among them.[[gvp]]
Four eruptions fall in the last 250 years. Two were driven by steam, in 1792 and in 1851. Two brought magma to the surface, from 1902 to 1905 and from 1929 to 1932.[[gvp]][[ovsm]]
